title: Big financial decisions
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:15Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: No bank point teaches the new point's idea of weighing income, interest rates, total cost over time and personal goals when choosing a car, rent versus buy, or a loan; the closest, Buying a home, covers only mortgages and ongoing costs, and Minor and major decisions covers planning for costly choices without the interest and income trade-offs.

draft.title: Big financial decisions
card: A big financial decision is a choice that involves a lot of money and lasts a long time, such as buying a car, renting or buying a home, or taking out a loan.
Income matters because it sets what a person can afford to repay. Interest rates matter because a higher rate makes a loan cost more.
Total cost over time is more than the price on the sticker. It includes interest, fees and running costs such as insurance, repairs and fuel.
Personal goals matter too. A person who wants to move cities soon may prefer renting, while someone planning to stay for years may prefer buying.
draft.remember: Weigh income, interest rates, total cost over time and personal goals together.

a.q: Which of these is part of the total cost of buying a car on a loan?
opts: The interest paid on the loan as well as the price
The price on the sticker only
The income the buyer earns each year
The buyer's goal of owning a car
a.why: Total cost over time adds interest and other costs to the price. Income and goals affect the decision, but they are not costs of the car.
a.clue: Total cost is more than the sticker price.

b.q: Leila is 24 and takes a job in Mildura for one year before she moves overseas. She is choosing between renting a flat and buying one. Which choice best fits her situation?
opts: Renting, because her goal is to stay only a short time
Buying, because owning is always cheaper than renting
Renting, because interest rates do not affect renters
Buying, because her income will rise when she moves
b.why: Her goal is a short stay, and buying a home has large costs that suit a longer stay. Buying is not always cheaper, and nothing in the case says her income will rise.
b.clue: Look at how long she plans to stay.

a.best: The interest paid on the loan as well as the price

b.best: Renting, because her goal is to stay only a short time
